reference: GNU coreutils whoami (independent executable found on the reference PATH); metadata contracts use Bash type/help builtins and the descriptions in the stock Bash whoami loadable source.
coverage: Default current-user output, end-of-options handling, and repeated calls in one Bash process.
GNU option behavior for operands, invalid options, --help, and --version; disagreements remain visible as FAIL.
Bash loadable metadata: type identifies whoami as a builtin and help exposes the source-documented description.
Regression checks expand aliases, end-of-options, option ordering and invalid/extra-operand statuses; banners use content/identity invariants.
exclusions: The runner supplies one passwd entry for its isolated identity, so an effective UID without an NSS/passwd name is deferred.
Only the documented stock Bash loadable contract and GNU coreutils option surface are covered.

cases.purpose: The no-operand invocation prints the name associated with the isolated current effective user.
A standalone -- ends option parsing and leaves no operand, so the identity is still printed.
Two calls in one shell each print one identity line, exercising repeated lookup and cached shell identity state.
GNU whoami rejects an operand; keep any status, diagnostic, or output difference from the loadable visible.
An unsupported short option must fail according to the GNU CLI oracle; preserve Bash loadable option-parser differences.
GNU branding and banner wording are excluded from byte parity. Check successful status, nonempty output and correct command identity, then compare only that invariant.
cases.script:
text=$(whoami --help)
[[ -n $text && $text == *'whoami'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'whoami --help succeeds with identified nonempty output'

cases.purpose: GNU branding and banner wording are excluded from byte parity. Check successful status, nonempty output and correct command identity, then compare only that invariant.
cases.script:
text=$(whoami --version)
[[ -n $text && $text == *'whoami'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'whoami --version succeeds with identified nonempty output'

cases.purpose: The statically compiled loadable is available as a Bash builtin even when candidate PATH is empty.
Bash help resolves the loadable and includes the independently documented stock-source summary and description.
cases.script: help_text=$(help whoami); [[ $help_text == *'Print user name'* && $help_text == *'Display name of current user.'* ]] && printf 'documented help available\n'

cases.purpose: Compare behavior when the effective UID has no passwd/NSS name, including GNU's diagnostic and the loadable's fallback behavior.
cases.reason: The harness provides a passwd entry for its sole isolated identity and does not let a fixture alter the read-only NSS files or select an unmapped effective UID. A future disposable VM or controlled identity/NSS mock must run GNU whoami and the candidate with the same unmapped UID and verify stdout, stderr, and status.
